q: Scripts create accounts and flood your Notes app with writes. Your rules are correct. What do you add?
why: App Check rejects requests that do not come from your genuine app; rules alone cannot tell a script from your app.

q: You turn on App Check enforcement on launch day. What is the likely result?
o: Users on older versions get errors
why: Enforcement rejects unverified requests. Watch the metrics first, then enforce one product at a time.

q: Which event parameter is fine to send to Analytics?
why: Send categories, never personal data such as text, emails or ids.

q: Photo uploads fail in production. What lets you hide the feature in minutes?
o: A feature flag in Remote Config
why: If the app already reads a flag with a default, you change the value in the console and apps pick it up on their next fetch.

q: Why does Crashlytics group crash reports into issues?
o: To show which problem hits most users
why: Grouping turns thousands of reports into a few issues, ranked by users affected, so you fix the biggest first.

q: You want a new reminder screen to reach users slowly and safely. Which approach fits best?
why: A rollout gives the new value to a small share first; you raise it while watching crashes and events, and can roll back.

q: Remote Config is a safe place to store an API secret because only your app fetches it.
why: Values reach the client, so anyone inspecting the app can read them. Keep secrets on a server.

q: In the lab, the app keeps working with its default value even when the fetch fails.
why: Defaults set in code are used until a fetch succeeds, which is also how the app behaves offline.
